Test Case Name: Login form displays correctly
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Observe the form
Expected Result:
Heading, username field, password field (masked), Sign in button (enabled), 
and Forgot password link (href=/forgot-password) are all visible

Test Case Name: Successful login with correct credentials
Precondition: Account is active, user exists in the system
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Enter correct username and password
3. Click Sign in
Test Data / Input:
Test data: validUser (login.json)
username: vet@example.com
password: password-password123
Expected Result: User is logged in, access/refresh tokens are stored, redirected to dashboard

Test Case Name: Login with wrong password for an existing user
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Enter correct username, wrong password
3. Click Sign in
Test Data / Input:
Test data: invalidUser (login.json)
username: vet@example.com
password: wrong-password
Expected Result: "Incorrect username or password." is shown, user stays on /login, submit button remains enabled

Test Case Name: Login with a username that does not exist
Precondition: Given username is not registered in the system
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Enter a non-existent username and any password
3. Click Sign in
Test Data / Input:
Test data: nonExistentUser (login.json)
username: doesnotexist@example.com
password: password-password123
Expected Result: "Incorrect username or password." is shown (same generic message as wrong password), user stays on /login

Test Case Name: Submitting login form with both fields empty
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Leave both fields empty
3. Click Sign in
Expected Result: "Username is required" and "Password is required" are shown, user stays on /login

Test Case Name: Submitting login form with empty username only
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Enter password only, leave username empty
3. Click Sign in
Expected Result: "Username is required" is shown, no request is sent, user stays on /login

Test Case Name: Submitting login form with empty password only
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Enter username only, leave password empty
3. Click Sign in
Expected Result: "Password is required" is shown, no request is sent, user stays on /login

Test Case Name: Login disabled after too many failed attempts
Precondition:
Multiple failed login attempts 
already made for this user (rate limit reached)
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Enter a valid username and any password
3. Click Sign in
Test Data / Input:
Mocked response: 429, header retry-after: 30, 
fixture throttled-error.json
Expected Result: Form shows throttled state (submit disabled / cooldown message), matching cy.expectThrottled behavior

Test Case Name: SQL injection attempt is safely rejected
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Enter SQL injection string in both username and password
3. Click Sign in
Expected Result:
Payload is sent as plain text (not executed), "Incorrect username or password."
 is shown, app does not crash, user stays on /login

Test Case Name: XSS attempt is safely rejected
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Enter <script>alert('xss')</script> as username
3. Click Sign in
Expected Result: Payload is sent as plain text and rendered as inert text on the page (React escapes it); none of the page's existing <script> tags contain the injected payload, "Incorrect username or password." is shown

Test Case Name: Disabled account shows same generic error as wrong credentials
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Enter valid username/password of a disabled account
3. Click Sign in
Test Data / Input:
Test data: validUser (login.json), mocked as 
401 login-invalid-credentials.json
Expected Result:
"Incorrect username or password." is shown (identical to wrong-password case, 
does not reveal account is disabled), user stays on /login

Test data: whitespaceOnlyUsername (login.json)
username: '   '
password: password-password123

"Username is required" is shown (username field is trimmed by the schema), 
no request is sent, user stays on /login

2. Enter valid username, only spaces as password
3. Click Sign in
Test Data / Input:
Test data: whitespaceOnlyPassword (login.json)
username: vet@example.com
password: '   '

which returns "Incorrect username or password."

Test Case Name: Username and password fields have associated visible labels
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Inspect the id of each input and the matching label[for] element
Expected Result: Each input has an id, and a visible <label for="..."> element exists referencing it

Test Case Name: Required fields are marked for assistive technology
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Inspect username and password input attributes
Expected Result: Both inputs have aria-required="true" (native HTML required attribute is not used by this form)

Test Case Name: All login controls are keyboard-focusable in logical order
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Focus username, password, and submit button individually
Expected Result: Username, password, and submit button are each natively focusable, in source/DOM order. Note: the username field autofocuses on page load.

Test Case Name: Login error is exposed to assistive technology via role="alert"
Steps:
1. Open /login
2. Submit invalid credentials
3. Inspect the error banner
Expected Result: Error banner is present with role="alert" and is visible, so screen readers announce it

Test Case Name: JWT contains correct role and clinic_id for an admin user
Precondition: Admin user exists, assigned to a clinic
Steps:
1. Generate token via MyTokenObtainPairSerializer.get_token(admin_user)
2. Inspect token claims
Expected Result: token['role'] == 'ADMIN', token['clinic_id'] == clinic_a.id, token['email'] == admin_user.email

Test Case Name: JWT contains correct claims for a vet-role user
Precondition: Vet user exists, assigned to a clinic
Steps:
1. Generate token via MyTokenObtainPairSerializer.get_token(vet_user)
2. Inspect token claims
Expected Result: token['role'] == 'VET', token['clinic_id'] == clinic_a.id

Test Case Name: JWT clinic_id is null when the user has no clinic
Precondition: Admin user exists with clinic set to None
Steps:
1. Set admin_user.clinic = None and save
2. Generate token
3. Inspect claims
Expected Result: token['clinic_id'] is None (does not crash or default to a wrong value)

Test Case Name: JWT claims differ between users from different clinics
Precondition: Two admin users exist in two different clinics
Steps:
1. Generate tokens for admin_user and other_clinic_admin
2. Compare clinic_id claims
Expected Result: token_a['clinic_id'] != token_b['clinic_id'] (claim is not hardcoded/shared)

Test Case Name: Session remains valid after a full page reload
Precondition: User is already authenticated (valid tokens in localStorage)
Steps:
1. Log in and land on /owners
2. Reload the page
Expected Result: User stays on /owners after reload, is not redirected to /login, /me request succeeds

Test Case Name: Stored access token is reused for subsequent API calls
Steps:
1. Log in and land on /owners
2. Navigate to /owners again (not a reload)
3. Inspect the outgoing request
Expected Result:
Request to the owners endpoint includes an Authorization: 
Bearer <token> header, login form is not shown again

Test Case Name: Unauthenticated visitor is redirected from a protected page to /login
Steps: 1. Directly visit /owners without logging in
Expected Result: User is redirected to /login

Test Case Name: User is redirected back to the originally requested page after login
Precondition: No tokens present, user attempts to visit a protected page
Steps:
1. Visit /owners (redirected to /login)
2. Log in with valid credentials
Expected Result: After successful login, user lands on /owners (not the default dashboard)

Test Case Name: Invalid/corrupted token is cleared instead of showing a broken page
Precondition: localStorage contains a malformed access/refresh token
Steps: 1. Visit /owners with an invalid token already set in localStorage
Expected Result: User is redirected to /login instead of seeing a broken protected page

Test Case Name: Logout clears local tokens and redirects to /login
Steps:
1. Log in and land on /owners
2. Click the logout button
Expected Result:
Logout request is sent with the refresh token, localStorage tokens 
are cleared, user is redirected to /login

Test Case Name: Local session is cleared even if the logout request fails
Steps:
1. Log in
2. Mock the logout endpoint to fail (500)
3. Click the logout button
Expected Result: Local tokens are still cleared and user is redirected to /login, despite the failed server call

Test Case Name: Protected pages are blocked again after logout
Precondition: User logged out in the previous step
Steps:
1. Log out
2. Attempt to visit /owners directly
Expected Result: User is redirected to /login, cannot access /owners with the old session

Test Case Name: Generic error message is shown on a 500 server error
Steps:
1. Mock the login endpoint to return 500
2. Submit valid credentials
Expected Result:
"The server encountered an error. Please try again." 
is shown (NOT the invalid-credentials message), submit button remains enabled

Test Case Name: Message is shown when the network is unreachable
Steps:
1. Force a network error on the login request (forceNetworkError)
2. Submit valid credentials
Expected Result: "Cannot reach the server. Check your connection and that the API is running." is shown

Test Case Name: Message is shown when the login request times out
Steps:
1. Delay the login response by 30s
2. Submit valid credentials
3. Wait
Expected Result: "The request timed out." is shown

Test Case Name: Submit button is not stuck in a loading state after a failed request
Steps:
1. Mock login endpoint to return 500
2. Submit valid credentials
3. Wait for the response
Expected Result: Submit button returns to enabled state, is not stuck disabled/loading

Test Case Name: Login form is usable on a mobile viewport
Steps:
1. Set viewport to a mobile size (e.g. iphone-x)
2. Check that all form elements are visible and usable
3. Complete a login
Expected Result: Form fields and submit button are visible, not cut off or overlapping, login completes successfully

Test Case Name: Login form is usable on a tablet viewport
Steps:
1. Set viewport to a tablet size (e.g. ipad-2)
2. Check layout and usability
Expected Result: Form remains usable and correctly laid out
